title: Exactness of the internal Hom in each variable
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X$ be a scheme and let
$K',K,K'',M,M',M''$ be complexes of $A$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. If
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ and $M'\to M\to M''\to M'[1]$ are
distinguished triangles of $D(X_{\Et},A)$, then the sequences

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A(K'',M)\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K',M)
\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K'',M)[1],
$$

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M')\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M'')
\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M')[1]
$$

are distinguished triangles. Here $X_{\Et}$ is the small étale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with the universe and small-skeleton convention
[def-weil-size-convention]; $A_X$ is its constant sheaf of commutative
rings and $D(X_{\Et},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$
[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The internal Hom is that of the ringed
site $(X_{\Et},A_X)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], computed by a
K-injective resolution of the second variable. The arrows use the
bifunctor's usual shift and sign identifications.

proof.text: Work directly on the recorded small etale site, whose object universe is u+1 and morphism universe is u [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Set R to the constant commutative ring sheaf A_X. The category in the statement is exactly its full module derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the existing independent-universe derivedInternalHomOfUniverses [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], without a change of site or coefficient category.

It supplies the target shift and triangulated structure directly, so the result has the exact conjunct order of the statement. No boundedness or finite-generation assumption or additional comparison is needed.

lean.statement: theorem sf_internalHom_triangulated (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (X : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of A))))] : (∀ M, ∃ _ : ((Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u + 1, w} X.smallEtaleTopology ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of A)))).flip.obj M).CommShift ℤ, ((Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u + 1, w} X.smallEtaleTopology ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of A)))).flip.obj M).IsTriangulated) ∧ (∀ K, ∃ _ : ((Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u + 1, w} X.smallEtaleTopology ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of A)))).obj (op K)).CommShift ℤ, ((Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u + 1, w} X.smallEtaleTopology ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of A)))).obj (op K)).IsTriangulated)
lean.note: The two conjuncts express the two image-triangle conclusions using Mathlib Functor.IsTriangulated and CommShift, in the same interface as ringedInternalHom_exact. The first uses the opposite pretriangulated category (negative shift); the second is covariant. The category is written literally as D(Mod(A_X)), as in the node, and the operation is the recorded derivedInternalHomOfUniverses specialized at the constant ring sheaf. Universes: site objects u+1, arrows u, coefficients and modules u+1, localization w. HasDerivedCategory is the structural localization parameter, with no extra mathematical finiteness assumption.
